text:
maria: Heads up — noticed our Next.js edge sample app ballooned +160KB after upgrading the JS SDK to 1.8.0 and now fails in Vercel edge with a runtime error.

alex: ugh. what error?

maria: ReferenceError: process is not defined, and the bundle includes a ton of node polyfill code (Buffer, process shim, crypto polyfill). bundle analyzer shows @redwood-inference/sdk/index.cjs pulling in whole lodash & node-libs.

jordan: do you have the import line you used?

maria: import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk';

alex: that's a default import into CJS entrypoint — many bundlers will conservatively include the entire cjs export surface. try the ESM entry if we publish one (module field) or a named import.

maria: tried `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk'` and it still pulled in stuff. looks like the package.json has sideEffects: true in the published tarball? or some file-level sideEffects comments.

sam: can you paste package.json from node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk?

maria: pulled it up quickly — it has "main": "dist/index.cjs.js", "module": "dist/index.esm.js", but there is no "sideEffects" key. also there is an index.js that re-exports everything with `module.exports = require('./dist/index.cjs')` (so interop shim present).

alex: ok that's the classic tree-shake failure: bundler sees a CommonJS-ish re-export and can't safely tree-shake named exports, so it pulls in whole module and the node polyfills. For edge runtimes that kills both size and runtime.

jordan: reproduction steps we use in sample-app: Next.js 13 edge function, esbuild (via next). If you `import` the default from the cjs wrapper, esbuild turns that into a require call and pulls polyfills.

maria: stacktrace in edge: `at Object../node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/shims/crypto.js` and then `ReferenceError: process is not defined`. build-bot also flagged increase in page payload.

build-bot: :warning: bundle-size/regression detected for /edge-sample (delta +160KB) — see CI artifact: https://ci.internal/artifacts/edge-sample/bundle-1768534444.html

sam: quick fixes for the app: 1) force ESM import path: `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/index.esm.js'` (not ideal) 2) use dynamic import in middleware and ensure the bundler treats it as ESM 3) pin to previous SDK 1.7.x for now.

alex: long-term we should: - publish a clean ESM entrypoint with no CJS wrapper (exports map) - add "sideEffects": false (or file-level exceptions) - ensure package exports map points `import` -> dist/index.esm.js and default `require` -> dist/index.cjs.js - avoid including node-only polyfills behind optional requires

jordan: also add a small note in the SDK README about edge runtime compatibility + bundler gotchas and a small sample Next.js edge snippet using the ESM path.

maria: I can PR the sample-app to use the explicit esm path as a stopgap. can someone from runtime team confirm if the SDK intentionally calls `require('crypto')` in code paths that run at import time?

alex: there is a tiny sync shim for signing in auth that lazily loads node crypto via `require`. if that require is in top-level module scope it will get bundled. should be changed to lazy/dynamic require inside runtime-only callsite.

sam: checklist for SDK change: 1) move any `require('node:*')` into function bodies (lazy) 2) add exports map entries and test with webpack/rollup/esbuild 3) publish a minor release and flag breaking note about edge bundle size 4) add unit test that uses esbuild to ensure no polyfill shims end up in ESM bundle

maria: i'll open an issue with reproduction + bundle analyzer HTML and link PR for sample-app. putting it on the 1.8.1 milestone.

alex: small nit — also run `npx modclean`/strip dev-only deps from the published tarball. sometimes source maps or leftover cjs files keep requiring polyfills.

jordan: for typings: TS consumers sometimes import `import SDK from '@redwood-inference/sdk'` and expect types to be on default export. if we change exports map we need to ensure types field points to `dist/index.d.ts` and that default vs named typing surfaces are clear. otherwise TS users will add `esModuleInterop` to workaround, which again might cause bundlers to include interop glue.

maria: agreed. i'll include a typings checklist in the issue. Also adding regression test to devex CI: build the edge sample with next + node 18 target and fail if bundle regresses >50KB.

sam: awesome. one more ask: can we add a small note in the changelog for 1.8.1 telling customers who use edge/deno/worker runtimes to import from `@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/index.esm.js` until we ship fix? saves support tickets.

maria: will do. thanks team :thumbsup:

alex: thanks — ping me on the PR review, I'll verify exports map and run esbuild test locally.

maria: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/478 — includes bundle analyzer and sample repro.

build-bot: :white_check_mark: CI test run for sample-app completed (regression check failed) — see pipeline 4821

jordan: linking this to docs task as well — docs/devex/edge-guide.md needs a short section about ESM import hygiene and sideEffects.

maria: filing docs todo. closing thread once PR is merged.
